postoffice_volunteer.text: Mind your head. The roof is the oldest saggy thing in Cornwall, apart from me.
This small manor house dates from the 1300s. The National Trust bought it in 1903 for 100 pounds.
In the 1840s it was the village post office, soon after the penny post began in 1840.
The slate roof is so heavy the ridge bows. It looks wonky but it has held for centuries.
